title: Source-local Q3 cutoff-tail scalar energy envelope
question: Can a cutoff tail restricted to one source-support edge be bounded by a source- and volume-independent fourth power of the local shifted Q3 potential, while finite matrix quotients are stress-tested separately?

finite_test.description: Scalar tests use arbitrary contractions u=a x and v=b y with |a|,|b|<=1; matrix tests use the registered smooth spectral cutoff on the source edge only.

mathematical_interface.contraction: For |u|<=|x| and |v|<=|y|, B(u,v)<= (c+lambda)*(1+x^4+y^4), and the same bound holds for B(x,y).
mathematical_interface.local_potential: For k_pot=1+v(x)+v(y)+2*d, the registered parameters satisfy S<=(8/g)*k_pot because 1+4*(r/g)^2-8/g<=0.
mathematical_interface.fourth_envelope: |T|^4 <= [16*(c+lambda)/g]^4*k_pot^4. This is a scalar potential-level envelope; it is not an operator inequality for the kinetic Hamiltonian.
mathematical_interface.qft_role: The result supplies a source-edge polynomial input for the OS/KMS-facing tail lane and isolates the remaining noncommutative Gibbs/domain step.

lean_crosscheck.role: R350 checks the exact rational scalar inequalities and fourth-power composition only; matrix quotients, Gibbs traces, operator domains and QFT limits remain Python evidence/open analysis.

adversarial_review.check: The scalar bound is used only under explicit |u|<=|x| and |v|<=|y|; the smooth spectral cutoff is checked separately as a contraction.
B is a sum of nonnegative terms for c,lambda>=0, so |B(x,y)-B(u,v)|<=B(x,y)+B(u,v) is legal; no monotonicity of B under contraction is assumed.
The estimate uses t^2<=(1+t^4)/2 before the quartic comparison, retaining the c contribution rather than dropping it.
The exact square completion carries the r<0 term and records the residual 1+4(r/g)^2-8/g, which is nonpositive for the inherited fixture.
The fourth-power constant is recomputed as [16(c+lambda)/g]^4 from the manifest inputs; it is not a pasted derived number.
The closed statement is scalar/potential-level only. The kinetic operator does not commute with the cutoff tail, so no operator order T^4<=C K^4 is inferred.
The scalar constant is local and source/volume independent, while finite matrix quotient rows are diagnostics and do not prove uniform Gibbs moments.
Matrix rows use the inherited cosine spectral cutoff on the selected edge; scalar rows cover every contraction, which is the only property used by the envelope.
R350 formalizes rational inequalities only and does not encode matrices, Gibbs traces, unbounded domains, OS reconstruction or thermodynamic limits.
The source-edge envelope does not close local Gibbs moments, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.
